steps.title: Select suitable DNA templates
steps.instruction: Choose only DNA extracts that have a concentration greater than 10 ng/µL and a 260/280 absorbance ratio above 1.7 for downstream PCR.

steps.title: Prepare master‑mastermix for all primers
steps.instruction: Combine the following reagents to make a 440 µL master‑mastermix that will be split among the six primer‑pair tubes: MgCl₂ (25 mM) 2.5 µL, dNTPs (10 mM) 114 µL, GoTaq DNA Polymerase 0.2 µL, 5× GoTaq Buffer 2.5 µL, BSA 114 µL, nuclease‑free H₂O 14.8 µL (adjust to reach a total of 440 µL). Vortex each component before pipetting and vortex the final mixture once it is assembled.

steps.title: Aliquot master‑mastermix into primer‑specific tubes
steps.instruction: Dispense 440 µL of the master‑mastermix into each of six 2 mL Eppendorf tubes. Label each tube with the corresponding primer‑pair name (V9, V3, V5‑V7S, V5‑V7L, V7, V7p+V8).

steps.title: Add primers to each primer‑specific tube
steps.instruction: To each of the six labeled tubes add 10 µL of 10 µM forward primer and 10 µL of 10 µM reverse primer for that pair. After addition the tube composition (T4) is: Forward primer 10 µL, Reverse primer 10 µL, MgCl₂ (25 mM) 50 µL, dNTPs (10 mM) 20 µL, GoTaq 4 µL, 5× Buffer 50 µL, BSA 20 µL, H₂O 296 µL, total 460 µL. Vortex the tube to mix.

steps.title: Distribute template to PCR wells
steps.instruction: In a set of 14 PCR tubes (or two rows of a 96‑well plate) add an excess of template to each well: pipette 20 µL of each DNA extract (including a positive control and a negative control consisting of the elution AE buffer) using a single‑channel 200 µL pipette set to 23 µL in four incremental steps, discarding any excess liquid. Change tips between primer‑pair rows. Then, using a multichannel 10‑100 µL pipette, add 2 µL of the same template to each well. Inspect tips visually to avoid aspirating air.

steps.title: Seal, vortex, and centrifuge PCR plates
steps.instruction: Cover each PCR plate with a cellophane seal using a plate press (6 seconds under pressure). Vortex the sealed plate at 1000 rpm for 10 seconds. Spin the plate in a benchtop manual plate centrifuge at 1000 rpm for 10 seconds (room temperature).

steps.title: Run PCR programs on thermocyclers
steps.instruction:
Place the V9‑barcode plate in one thermal cycler and the V3, V5‑V7S, V5‑V7L, V7, and V7p+V8 plates in a second thermal cycler. Use the following programs:
• T5A (V9): 95 °C 2 min; 30 cycles of 95 °C 30 s, 48 °C 45 s, 72 °C 1 min; final extension 72 °C 5 min.
• T5B (all other barcodes): 95 °C 2 min; 30 cycles of 95 °C 30 s, 54 °C 1 min, 72 °C 1 min; final extension 72 °C 5 min.
Any standard PCR instrument (e.g., SimpliAmp, Applied Biosystems A24811) may be used.

steps.title: Post‑PCR vortex and spin down
steps.instruction: After the run, vortex the plates again at 1000 rpm for 10 seconds and spin down in the benchtop centrifuge (1000 rpm, 10 seconds). Remove the cellophane seal.

steps.title: Perform agarose gel electrophoresis
steps.instruction: Set the power supply to 125 V, 500 mA and run for 45 minutes. Load 6 µL of a 100 bp DNA ladder on the left side of each row (two ladders per gel). Using an adjustable‑spacer multichannel pipette, load 5 µL of each PCR product into the corresponding wells (well spacing 6.25 mm, plate spacing 9 mm). Run the gel, place it under UV illumination, photograph, and print. Expect a band in every well except the negative control, with band sizes matching the expected amplicon lengths for each primer pair.

steps.title: Purify PCR products with ExcelaPure plates
steps.instruction: Warm nuclease‑free water to 56 °C. Add 55 µL of this water to each PCR well (excluding controls and any failed reactions) using a multichannel 20‑200 µL pipette with filter tips; mix by pipetting up‑and‑down ~5 times. Transfer the entire mixture to the corresponding well of an ExcelaPure™ 96‑Well UF PCR Purification Plate (Catalog #36181, Edge Bio).

steps.title: Elute purified DNA and incubate
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the purification plate with a collection plate underneath at 5000 rpm for 7 minutes (room temperature). Add 50 µL of 56 °C water to each well, mix by pipetting up‑and‑down ~15 times (change tips each time), and incubate at 56 °C for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Transfer purified DNA to final plate
steps.instruction: Label a new 96‑well PCR plate, drawing lines between each pair of rows to separate primer‑pair groups (V3‑V9). Mix each well of the purification plate by pipetting up‑and‑down ~15 times, then transfer the eluate to the corresponding well of the final plate. Change tips for every transfer.

steps.title: Seal final plate and store
steps.instruction: Cover the final plate with a cellophane seal using the plate press (6 seconds under pressure) and store the sealed plate at –20 °C.

steps.title: Quantify purified amplicons with Qubit HS
steps.instruction:
Using a Qubit 2.0 Fluorometer (catalog Q33226) and the Qubit HS assay, prepare assay tubes as follows:
• Standards: 190 µL of Qubit HS master mix + 10 µL of each standard; vortex, incubate 1 min.
• Samples: 198 µL of Qubit HS master mix + 2 µL of purified PCR product; vortex, incubate 1 min.
Read fluorescence and record the concentration (ng/µL) for each well.

steps.title: Calculate template and water volumes for pooling
steps.instruction:
For each sample, identify the lowest concentration among its barcode amplicons (exclude any barcode with <2 ng/µL, the minimum required by YCGA). Use the molar correction factors (V9 0.5, V5‑V7S 0.5, V3 0.6, V7 0.6, V7p+V8 0.9, V5‑V7L 1.0) to compute:
Template volume (µL) = (50 µL ÷ Qubit ng/µL) × correction factor.
Water volume (µL) = (50 µL × correction factor) – template volume.
Record the calculated volumes for each barcode in the pooling plate.

steps.title: Prepare pooling plate with calculated volumes
steps.instruction: Set up a new 96‑well PCR plate labeled for pooling. For each well, add the calculated amount of water first, then add the calculated amount of purified amplicon template. Change pipette tips after every addition to avoid cross‑contamination.

steps.title: Pool amplicons into labeled 2 mL tubes
steps.instruction: Label 2 mL Eppendorf tubes with extraction number, siphonophore genus, the text “GC DNA pooled”, and your initials. Using a multichannel 20‑200 µL pipette, combine the amplicons for each sample according to the pooling layout. If the total volume exceeds a single row, create two semi‑pools (V9 + V5‑V7S + V3 in one, V7 + V7p+V8 + V5‑V7L in the other). Then, with a single‑channel 20‑200 µL pipette, transfer each pooled mixture into its corresponding labeled 2 mL tube. Vortex briefly, close caps, and store the tubes at –20 °C.
